data.title: Stock Futures Hold Near Flat as Anthropic Prices IPO at $83 Ahead of Debut
data.description: According to CNBC, U.S. equity futures were near flat Wednesday night as traders looked ahead to Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut Thursday under the ticker “ANT.” A person familiar with the matter said Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above the expected range. Dow futures rose 35 points, or 0.07%, while S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures each added 0.1%. In Wednesday’s regular session, the Dow fell more than 560 points, or 1.1%, the S&P 500 lost 0.2% for a fifth consecutive decline, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.4%.

data.title: Neel Kashkari: Massive AI Investment Poses Concentration Risk to the Economy
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari said large-scale investment in artificial intelligence poses concentration risks to the U.S. economy. He said AI investment had been a major driver of U.S. economic growth in recent years, but could slow, potentially sharply, if it fails to boost productivity as expected or deliver the returns investors anticipate. He said economic growth would slow as a result.

Kashkari said it remains unclear whether AI will generate stronger productivity growth or other returns. He said he was optimistic about AI's prospects but urged openness to different outcomes, including the possibility that some investments could be misguided. He added that AI infrastructure construction is not the only factor driving inflation.

data.title: Nvidia to Move Pay Raises and New Equity Awards Forward to December
data.description: According to Sina Finance, Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress promised employees pay raises and additional equity benefits in December at a companywide meeting on Wednesday, media reported, citing people familiar with the meeting. Nvidia will move the raises and new equity awards to December, breaking with its usual practice of conducting annual employee reviews in the spring.

data.title: NEAR Approves HSP-029 Proposal to Cap Issuance at 1.6% Within 24 Months
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, NEAR has approved HSP-029, a proposal to cap its token issuance rate at 1.6% within 24 months. The proposal includes a one-quarter grace period. Token issuance will only be reduced after validators individually upgrade and adopt the new rules.

data.title: Blockaid Flags More Than 8,800 GTA-Themed Solana Tokens in Four Months
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Blockaid, the blockchain security firm flagged more than 8,800 Solana tokens themed around Grand Theft Auto over four months. The flags covered tokens classified as malicious, risk warnings, and spam. Blockaid said the tokens use the GTA theme to attract users with fake presales and airdrops, then direct them to wallet drainers that can steal assets.

data.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella Warns Outages May Be More Than Temporary Glitches
data.description: According to Jin10, Microsoft (MSFT.O) CEO Satya Nadella warned, according to The Wall Street Journal, that service disruptions may be more than temporary glitches.

data.title: Senators Press Treasury to Ensure ‘Equal Footing’ for Stablecoin Issuers in GENIUS Act
data.description: Bipartisan senators urged Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to give state-regulated stablecoin issuers a safe harbor under the GENIUS Act, saying they need “equal footing” with federal regulators. In a letter, Sens. Cynthia Lummis, Kirsten Gillibrand, Angela Alsobrooks, Pete Ricketts, Kevin Cramer and Mark Warner said Treasury’s proposal protects pending federal applicants if granted a waiver but offers no equivalent to state issuers, according to The Block. The act lets issuers with $10 billion or less choose state oversight if rules are substantially similar; states must certify alignment by January 2028. New York and Wyoming were cited as having comprehensive rules. Some senators raised the issue in June; the OCC’s final rule is set to take effect in January.

data.title: AI | Parmy Olson: Anthropic Could Pursue $30 Trillion by Expanding Into Industries
data.description: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Parmy Olson says expanding deeper into healthcare, law, finance and cybersecurity is one way Anthropic could pursue the $30 trillion in potential revenue Dario Amodei has said awaits. Anthropic has warned that as it expands, it may increasingly compete with some of its customers, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Cybersecurity Stocks Rally as Wall Street Buys Protection From AI Risks
data.description: Cybersecurity stocks rose during the November 18 session as the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.13%, with Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and CrowdStrike (CRWD) posting substantial gains. The move echoed a September rally tied by Dow Jones to debate over AI risks, according to BeInCrypto. Yahoo Finance’s top U.S. gainers list on November 19 included 15 security or network-infrastructure firms among 25 stocks. Palo Alto reported that next-generation security annual recurring revenue jumped 66% to $9.73 billion and raised its full-year profit guidance, but shares fell after the earnings release. The company also authorized a $1 billion buyback through 2027, equal to 0.36% of its market value, and announced plans to acquire Applied Compute to offer enterprise customers secure open-weight AI models. In September, CEO Nikesh Arora said awareness of weaponized AI was growing; Dow Jones reported that OpenAI models breached AI company Hugging Face. In crypto, hacks drained more than $606 million from protocols in the first 18 days of April 2026, the worst month for exploits since February 2025. Whether AI drove the losses remains contested: Wasabi Protocol lost over $5 million in an admin-key compromise, which Blockaid traced to one admin wallet, while the AI-driven hacker theory resurfaced. The Drift Protocol and KelpDAO hacks totaled $577 million, but neither was a code exploit, according to a review of 2026 DeFi losses. DeFi total value locked had fallen 39% in 2026 by late June.

data.title: Nvidia Tells Staff It Is Leaving the Huang Era Behind
data.description: Nvidia told employees it is moving on from the era of longtime leader Jensen Huang, according to Bloomberg. At a town-hall meeting Wednesday, interim Chief Executive Officer Colette Kress reiterated her confidence in the company following Huang’s ouster.

data.title: Moody’s Shifts Nvidia Credit Outlook to Stable From Positive
data.description: Moody’s Ratings lowered its outlook on Nvidia Corp.’s credit to stable from positive, citing the resignation of longtime CEO Jensen Huang and the company’s lack of a formal succession plan, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Brookfield-Backed Scientific Games Sees Earnings Fall, Buys Back Bonds
data.description: According to Bloomberg, earnings at Brookfield-backed lottery business Scientific Games Holdings LP fell last quarter, and the company bought back bonds. One-time costs tied to delayed contract completions contributed to the decline, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

data.title: Gonka Cross-Chain Bridge Exploited, 22 Million Unbacked WGNK Minted
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Blockaid, Gonka’s cross-chain bridge was attacked, with the exploit minting 22 million WGNK tokens that were not backed by assets. Ethereum records show the attacker withdrew 884,151 USDT and 648 USDC from the bridge.

data.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella: Software Engineering Remains Vibrant and Will Thrive
data.description: According to Jin10, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said, “We are recognizing anew that software engineering remains vibrant and will thrive in the future.”

data.title: KPMG Canada Breach Led to Access of Client Tax Documents Amid Hack Spate
data.description: A cybersecurity breach at KPMG Canada resulted in access to some client tax documents amid a spate of hacks, Bloomberg reported.

data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Moody's said its rating reflects Nvidia's strong financial performance and market-leading position in AI data center computing and networking.

data.title: Challenger Turns Down Daiichi Life’s Revised $4.4 Billion Takeover Offer
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Challenger Ltd. rejected a revised A$6.5 billion ($4.4 billion) takeover offer from Daiichi Life Group Inc., marking the Japanese insurer’s second rejection in a month.

data.title: New York FX: Dollar Rises as Pound Hits Near One-Year Low After UK Inflation Data
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, the dollar rose against most G10 currencies as traders maintained bets on further Federal Reserve rate hikes despite a sharp drop in oil prices. The pound fell to its lowest level in nearly a year.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index gained 0.3%, rebounding after a decline on Tuesday, while Brent crude fell below $92 a barrel.

Sterling fell as much as 0.6% to $1.3136 against the dollar. UK inflation data released Wednesday prompted traders to reduce bets on further Bank of England rate hikes.

The euro fell 0.2% to $1.0979. The dollar was little changed at 159.32 yen, while the Australian dollar fell 0.2% to $0.6721.
